newsitem.title: ITALY: Foreign banks said interested in Napoli.
newsitem.headline: Foreign banks said interested in Napoli.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Landesbank, Britain's Natwest and the Netherlands' Rabobank are thought to be considering separate bids for control of Banco di Napoli, Italian newspapers reported on Tuesday.
The Italian Treasury has put 60 percent of the ailing bank up for auction and interest parties have until December 20 to make offers.
Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said that a number of foreign banks were believed to be showing interest in acquiring the southern Italian bank.
"Among the names which are most widely mentioned are those of Bayerische Landesbank, England's Natwest and the Dutch Rabobank," the newspaper said.
Italy's state-controlled Banca Nazionale di Lavoro and insurer INA said on Monday they had formally expressed joint interest in Banco di Napoli.
BNL president Mario Sarcinelli indicated to financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore on Sunday that if INA and BNL made a joint offer, INA would put up much of the cash and BNL would supply know-how.
INA is controlled by banks Istituto Bancario San Paolo Di Torino, IMI and Cariplo.

The BNL-INA bid is the only public expression of interest to date. Banco Ambrosiano Veneto and Banca Commerciale Italiano had previously indicated they might be interested in Banco di Napoli, but both groups have now said no.

Banco di Napoli unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.0 billion) in 1995 and plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year thanks largely to a poor, highly politicised loan policy.
The Treasury has installed new management at the firm and has promised to take on the bulk of the company's stock of bad debt before selling the group.
